posts.title: The Download: Jensen Huang’s open-source dilemma and cognitive immortality
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has attracted more than 115,000 signatures, including Elon Musk, but comb through the names, and…
bullets: The US government has tightened export controls to close loopholes allowing Chinese firms to access advanced AI chips via remote cloud services abroad.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces a credibility crisis within the open-source AI community, as new US regulations and chip-tracking requirements complicate his role as an industry advocate.
Data center emissions from US hyperscalers have tripled since 2018, reaching levels comparable to the total CO2 output of Denmark, highlighting the massive environmental cost of current AI scaling.

posts.title: Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
posts.summary: The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration. Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. The water can be released through turbines, generating electricity on demand. But an…
bullets: Hydropower generation in the US Southwest dropped 28% below the 10-year average between April and August 2026 due to persistent drought conditions.
Critical reservoirs Lake Powell and Lake Mead are hovering near minimum operating levels, threatening the reliability of a power source that served over 2 million people in 2025.
Climate change is increasing the volatility of regional water supplies, forcing a reevaluation of hydropower as a stable renewable energy asset in drought-prone areas.

posts.title: BYD marks its 32nd anniversary, from making batteries in Shenzhen to building cars overseas
posts.summary:
BYD started in a rented factory in Shenzhen and entered the auto industry through an acquisition in 2003.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD celebrated its 32nd anniversary, having grown from a small Shenzhen battery startup into a global NEV leader with over 19 million units produced.
The company's international expansion is accelerating, with exports surging 93.75% year-on-year in the first 10 months of 2026.
Despite strong export growth, BYD faces domestic headwinds, with sales in China declining 27.81% during the same period.
BYD is deepening its overseas footprint by increasing local sourcing and R&D efforts at its manufacturing hubs in Thailand and Brazil.

posts.title: Defect-Aware Chiplet Matching For Heterogeneous Integration Yield (ASU, Ampere)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Arizona State University and Ampere Computing published “DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration.” Abstract “Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited... » read more
The post Defect-Aware Chiplet Matching For Heterogeneous Integration Yield (ASU, Ampere) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from ASU and Ampere Computing introduced DT-MATCH, a framework designed to optimize yield in heterogeneous integration by accounting for chiplet defects and interconnect constraints.

The framework utilizes two distinct strategies: an integer linear programming (ILP) approach for maximum yield optimality and a greedy randomized adaptive search procedure (GRASP) for faster, high-efficiency computation.
By effectively managing lane-level defects and limited spare resources, this methodology addresses critical bottlenecks in assembling functional system-on-chip (SoC) designs from repairable chiplets.

posts.title: Backside Clock Mesh Reduces Skew And Power In Backside Power Delivery (KAIST)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) published “Clock Distribution Network with Backside Clock Mesh in BSPDN Architecture.” Abstract Excerpt “We propose a clock distribution network (CDN) in which the clock mesh is located on backside metal (BM) layers, while the rest of the network remains on the frontside. Since the backside... » read more
The post Backside Clock Mesh Reduces Skew And Power In Backside Power Delivery (KAIST) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: KAIST researchers proposed a novel clock distribution network (CDN) that integrates a clock mesh into the backside metal (BM) layers alongside the backside power delivery network (BSPDN).
The design addresses the complex challenge of managing keep-out zones (KOZs) between clock- and power-nTSVs by employing a potential-field method (PFM) for optimized placement.
This architecture aims to reduce clock skew and power consumption, providing a critical optimization path for advanced nodes utilizing backside power delivery.
